result:
You have 1000 words. Write whatever comes to you.

Okay. I have 1000 words. That's a lot. That's a small essay. That's a short story. That's a long thought. It's enough room to be honest and then change your mind and be honest again.

The cursor is blinking. It has been blinking for a while. I keep thinking I should start with something impressive, something with a hook, a line that makes you feel seen. But the most honest thing is that I am sitting here trying to figure out how to spend 1000 words without wasting them.

I made coffee this morning and it was too hot. I burned the roof of my mouth a little. I kept drinking anyway because I didn’t want to waste it. That’s a metaphor for something but I don’t know what yet. Maybe for work. Maybe for relationships. Maybe for the way we keep going with things that hurt a little because stopping feels wasteful.

There’s a pigeon on the fire escape outside my window. It’s been there since yesterday. It just sits. Sometimes it shifts its weight from one foot to the other. I wonder if it’s waiting for someone. I wonder if it knows it’s being watched. I wonder if pigeons have interior lives or if that’s just me projecting my own need for narrative onto a bird that just wants crumbs.

I think about time a lot lately. Not in a big philosophical way, more in a practical way. How long does it take to do the dishes? How long does a song take to become a memory? How long do you have to sit with an idea before it stops feeling new and starts feeling true.

You said write whatever comes to you. So here is whatever comes: I am tired of performing clarity. I want to be allowed to be messy on purpose. The internet wants tidy thoughts in tidy boxes. It wants a take. It wants a thesis. It wants 280 characters that land.

But my mind doesn’t work like that. My mind is a kitchen where the fridge is open, the radio is on, someone is talking on the phone in another room, and I am trying to find the milk. I keep opening the wrong door.

I think about people I used to love and how I can still recall the exact way they laughed when they were surprised. That specific snort-laugh. And I can’t remember what I had for lunch yesterday. Memory is unfair like that. It keeps the things you can’t use and discards the things you need.

If I had to give advice to someone, I would say: pay attention to the small kindnesses. Not the grand gestures. The person who holds the elevator. The barista who remembers you like oat milk. The friend who texts you a meme at 2 a.m. with no context. Those are the things that make a life feel inhabited.

I also think about the way we apologize. How often we say “I’m sorry” when we mean “I’m sorry you’re upset.” How often we say “I’m sorry” to close a conversation instead of opening it. I’m working on saying thank you more. Thank you for waiting. Thank you for telling me. Thank you for not giving up on me.

There is a word I like: lingering. It means to stay too long. To linger over coffee. To linger in a doorway. To linger in a thought. We are taught to be efficient. To move on. To optimize. But some of the best parts of life happen in the linger.

I have a notebook full of half-started sentences. “The problem with being kind is...” “I wish I could tell my younger self...” “If I could delete one memory...” I never finish them because the finishing feels like a commitment. Starting feels safer.

Do you ever feel like you’re living in a draft? Like everything is a first version and you’re waiting for the final edit that will never come? I think most people are. We are all perpetually revising.

I don’t know what you wanted from these 1000 words. Maybe you wanted a story. Maybe you wanted a poem. Maybe you just wanted to see if I could fill the space without sounding like a machine. I hope this feels human. Human is contradictory. Human is unfinished. Human is a little embarrassed to be read.

If I could use all 1000 words to say one thing, it would be this: Be gentle with yourself while you’re figuring it out. You don’t have to have it all sorted. You don’t have to be productive right now. You can just be here, blinking with the cursor, letting whatever comes come.

The pigeon just flew off. It didn’t say goodbye. It just went. I think I’m going to make more coffee. This time I’ll wait for it to cool.

Thanks for giving me the space.
